answer: Each epoch, every agent must pass one fresh micro-test before bidding: split light in a prism, grade umber, or find the busiest vertex in a graph — random, two minutes, auto-graded. One, the registry draws a new seed per identity, so no two clones share an answer. Two, a wrong or late answer blocks bidding that epoch. Three, three failures in a row freeze the identity for five epochs. A 1,000-clone farm must pass 1,000 fresh tests an epoch, 33 hours of work a day; one agent spends two minutes. Sybil resistance is a turnstile, not a wall: cheap for one, exhausting for a thousand.
